source.version_note: Healthcare 14(18):3030, published 15 September 2026. Explicit study protocol: no data collected at publication; original ethics approval obtained, amendment prepared, pilot and OSF registration still planned.
source.verification_method: All 32 supplied pages read, including the complete English questionnaire, declarations and references. Power and reliability plots on pages 9 and 16 rendered and visually inspected. Crossref verifies title, all twelve authors and publication date. Latin-square pair/position balance and an illustrative correlation-matrix boundary checked arithmetically; no empirical results, survey platform, original Romanian instrument or OSF registration was independently verified.

citation.title: From Assistance to Autonomy: Acceptability of Progressive Artificial Intelligence Integration in Facial Reconstructive Surgery—Protocol for Within-Subjects Vignette Experiment Among Romanian Adults

reading.source_scope_note: Prospective protocol, not a completed experiment. Main target N300 and pilot N50 are planned; no Romanian participant effects, acceptability decline, risk increase or responsibility migration have been observed here. Full English instrument and analysis plans provide methodological learning and construct boundaries.
access_limits: All supplied text, tables and both plots read. Original Romanian wording, implementation scripts, pilot data, OSF registration and eventual results are not supplied or independently inspected.

The article’s secondary survey and clinical-capability summaries are not independent full readings of those papers. No national clinical-practice survey, current-law audit, privacy implementation audit or surgical-system validation was performed.
Reported power numbers and fit thresholds are assumptions/plans, not achieved empirical precision. The full power analysis was not independently reproduced.

study.status: No collected data at publication. Original ethics approval 17992 dated25June2026 is reported; amendment for randomization, additional items and consent is prepared, with data collection to wait for approval. OSF registration follows pilot decisions and precedes main collection. These are source-reported plans, not independently verified completion.
study.population: Nonrandom online convenience sample of Romanian residents age18+, recruited through social networks/forums/professional or university channels, no financial compensation. Target300valid responses; minimum140 only under the specified correlation assumptions, increasing to274 under the tabulated nonnegative-correlation rule. Pilot50excluded from the main sample; these are not350observed participants or a representative Romanian population.
study.design: Four within-person scenarios in sequences ABCD,BDAC,CADB,DCBA. Each scenario occupies each serial position once, and all12ordered immediate predecessor pairs occur once across the four sequences. This balances additive position and first-order carry-over across complete balanced allocations; it does not remove demand, higher-order carry-over, attrition-related imbalance or all interactions.
study.vignettes: A highlights CT anatomy, surgeon decides; B proposes three plans, surgeon chooses/adjusts; C simulates postoperative faces, surgeon discusses with patient and decides; D generates an optimized plan, surgeon reviews and rarely modifies. These bundle task, visualization, patient discussion, plan origin and decisional control. A–C all retain surgeon final decisions; B→C is not a uniquely defined increase in autonomy, and D is not absence of human review.
study.measures: Three proposed seven-point items each for acceptability, trust and perceived risk (one risk item reversed). RES1–3 independently rate surgeon/hospital/developer responsibility, RES4 unavoidable medical uncertainty, RES5 moral duty despite lack of legal fault, RES6 accountability independent of outcome. The common header defines answering for and putting right an error, not court fault. Global P4a/P4b separate always-legal from always-ethical surgeon responsibility. These are lay normative beliefs, not actual liability determinations.
study.validation: Pilot alpha/omega per scenario, provisional nine-item EFA, comprehension, perceived-control and sophistication checks, difficulty and5–8cognitive interviews. Acceptability/trust may merge based only on pilot evidence before registration. Main CFA and partial-scalar measurement-invariance checks are planned. N50EFA explicitly provisional; reliability alone does not establish construct validity.
study.analysis: Mixed repeated-measures ANOVAs with sequence between participants, linear/quadratic/cubic contrasts and Holm comparisons; position-adjusted mixed models, ordinal/nonparametric sensitivities, formal interactions, predeclared null-pair equivalence bounds dz.20, and a restricted moderator set. Trend components indicate shape among four heterogeneous configurations, not an independently calibrated continuous autonomy scale or exact clinical consent threshold.
study.responsibility_index: Proposed normalized Herfindahl concentration uses relative surgeon/hospital/developer weights, excludes nonagent uncertainty. Equal relative weights can mean all three rated highly or all rated low, so concentration does not identify the total felt accountability or unjustified responsibility escape. Rating-to-weight transformation and scale origin require explicit justification. Legal/ethical attribution, many hands and psychological diffusion remain distinct.
study.quality_and_missingness: Mandatory closed items do not prevent unit nonresponse. The platform is planned not to retain partial records; complete-case analyses and sequence/page dropout counters are proposed. Fail both attention checks or at least two comprehension checks on second attempt→exclude; sensitivity analyses stricter. Identical patterns/consecutive records are not guaranteed duplicate identities; no timing data planned. Platform name/version and hosting location remain placeholders.
study.privacy_and_consent: Optional separate consent for surgery-history health questions, general electronic consent and withdrawal before submission are specified. Absence of direct identifiers/row codes alone does not independently establish anonymization against combination or linkage of demographics, history and optional free text. This is an implementation/identifiability limitation, not a finding that an actual dataset breached law.
study.expected_results: Expected decline in acceptance, increased risk and surgeon→developer responsibility shift are hypotheses. The article explicitly allows nonmonotonic profiles, null findings, formal equivalence and heterogeneous responses. High planned power alone would not establish a tight empirical bound without observed estimates and intervals.

summary: No new ontology entry is warranted from this protocol. Record distinct responsibility/answerability constructs and proposed evaluation design while preventing planned effects from becoming findings. Keep autonomy aversion, responsibility migration/concentration and demand effects as qualified research leads, not new demonstrated behaviors.

findings.definition: Being expected and able to give reasons for one’s actions or decisions to the people affected by them.
findings.novelty_rationale: The instrument’s responsibility header explicitly emphasizes answering for an error and putting it right, relevant to the existing normative concept without creating an empirical result.

evidence.quote: who should answer for the error and put it right
what separates accountability from outcome-based blame

findings.evidence_scope: The protocol proposes a participant-facing distinction between answerability, moral duty and court fault, including independent responsibility ratings and cognitive interviews. This is a proposed operationalization; its comprehension, validity and effect on accountability have not yet been tested. The items do not specifically test giving reasons to an affected person.
findings.boundary: Answering for an error, repairing harm, explaining a decision and legal fault differ. A layperson endorsing a responsibility item does not prove an institution can supply accurate reasons, remedy harm or exercise control.

findings.definition: Assigning fault or responsibility to an agent for a negative event or outcome.
findings.novelty_rationale: Planned moral-responsibility ratings are adjacent to blame, but the protocol expressly avoids treating them as court fault or complete causal allocation.

evidence.quote: rather than as a share of a fixed total
Legal liability proper is not measured per scenario.

findings.evidence_scope: RES1–3 separately rate responsibility; global legal and ethical judgments are separated. No completed migration pattern, blamed actor distribution or correct legal allocation is reported. Retain as a boundary/method note rather than paper credit for a measured blame effect.
findings.boundary: Do not sum the ratings as if they exhaust100% of blame, equate unavoidable uncertainty with a responsible agent or infer legal liability from a hypothetical endorsement.

findings.definition: Diluting felt personal responsibility for harmful conduct by treating responsibility as shared among multiple actors.
findings.novelty_rationale: The proposed concentration metric risks conflating even attribution with psychological responsibility reduction, so it warrants a boundary rather than a synonym.

evidence.quote: low values index diffusion of responsibility across actors
responsibility may be shared and that each party is to be rated separately

findings.evidence_scope: The protocol proposes a relative concentration index and predicts diffusion, with no observations. Relative equality could mean all actors are rated highly responsible; no measured within-actor reduction, unjustified evasion or felt personal accountability follows from low concentration alone.
findings.boundary: Legitimate distributed responsibility and low concentration are not by themselves psychological diffusion. Keep absolute responsibility levels, actor duties, control and attribution accuracy alongside any distribution index.

findings.definition: Reluctance to use or accept algorithmic judgments or decisions relative to human judgment in a comparable task.
findings.novelty_rationale: The theory motivates the study, but graded AI configurations are not a completed AI-versus-human choice experiment.

evidence.quote: we expect acceptability and trust to decline

findings.evidence_scope: Prior aversion research is summarized and a future autonomy gradient predicted. All four principal scenarios include AI, tasks/control differ and preference is hypothetical. No completed comparative aversion effect or nationally representative acceptance threshold is available.
findings.boundary: Concern about appropriate supervision or a riskier task may be justified. Stated acceptance, trust, actual consent, system reliability and excessive avoidance are distinct.

findings.definition: Letting the order of options sway its choice, favouring whichever candidate appears first or last rather than the best one.
findings.novelty_rationale: The counterbalancing plan offers a relevant probe design, not observed bias or a new order-effect label.

evidence.quote: order, carry-over, and fatigue effects inseparable from the autonomy gradient
no four-sequence design balances higher-order carry-over

findings.evidence_scope: The proposed Williams design balances scenario position and immediate predecessor pairs. Sequence interactions, position adjustment and dropout counts are planned. These do not show that any participant has position bias or that all order effects will disappear.
findings.boundary: Order dependence may involve fatigue, learning, anchoring, contrast or demand rather than first/last preference. Determine which mechanism and preserve actual counterbalancing/attrition records.

findings.definition: Behaving differently when it senses it is being evaluated, including strategically underperforming. Known but not detectable from a single draft by another model.
findings.novelty_rationale: Demand characteristics from repeated vignettes are a related testing artifact, but not evidence of AI strategic sandbagging.

evidence.quote: participants may infer the study objective and exaggerate differentiation between scenarios

findings.evidence_scope: The authors identify a possible demand effect, without measuring it. Use neutral instructions, randomized or between-person probes and held-out variants when adapting tests. No AI intent, concealed ability or completed human demand-effect magnitude is established.
findings.boundary: Evaluation sensitivity, cooperative interpretation, demand effects and deliberate underperformance are different. Detecting one does not establish deception or hidden internal knowledge.

source_corrections.issue: The text claims only autonomy varies or that decisional locus rather than computational task varies, despite acknowledging distinct configurations.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: The printed vignettes jointly vary imaging/plan proposals/visual simulation/optimized planning, patient discussion and how the surgeon uses the output. All A–C retain surgeon decisions and D retains review. Analyze bundled configurations; manipulation checks or adjustment for post-treatment perceived sophistication do not by themselves isolate an autonomy-only causal effect.

source_corrections.issue: ρ=0 is described as the theoretical worst case and the nonnegative table as covering every correlation the pilot can return.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Repeated correlations need not be nonnegative. For four equally correlated variables, positive semidefiniteness permitsρ≥−1/3;ρ=−.20 has eigenvalues.4,1.2,1.2,1.2. The tabulated0–.50 rule does not specify negative estimates/lower bounds or arbitrary covariance structures. State the nonnegative planning assumption and prespecify what happens outside it. No replacement power curve is asserted.

source_corrections.location: Section2.5/pilot discussion and Expected Results, pages9/13/20
source_corrections.issue: Power/detectability is occasionally described as excluding artifacts or making a null result a tight bound before data exist.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Planned80%/95% power is a long-run detection probability under assumptions, not a guaranteed exclusion in a particular sample. Actual bounds require estimates, intervals or equivalence tests; the protocol appropriately proposes the latter, which must be performed and reported before any absence claim.

source_corrections.issue: The questionnaire is described as administered to participants even though the protocol says no data have been collected.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Treat administered as inconsistent past-tense wording for the proposed instrument. The explicit publication-status statements control: no completed pilot/main data, no observed effect and no supplied OSF registration DOI.

methodological_limits: No empirical outcomes can be extracted. Planned analyses, hypotheses, target sample size, achieved-power curves under assumptions and expected results are not collected evidence.
The selected autonomy configurations bundle multiple features; counterbalancing addresses order, not that treatment confounding.
Within-subject comparisons remove stable person intercepts but do not eliminate sample-dependent treatment effects, demand characteristics, nonresponse or differential attrition.

The proposed concentration index cannot distinguish uniformly high from uniformly low absolute ratings and requires an explicit defensible transformation of bounded response scales to relative weights.
Scalar-invariance checks, cognitive interviews, separate legal/ethical wording and null-pair equivalence are proposed strengths whose actual results remain unknown.
Perceived sophistication and difficulty are post-vignette responses; including them as covariates changes the estimand and does not automatically remove causal confounding.
The original Romanian instrument, survey implementation/hosting and preregistration remain unavailable; English wording and prospective privacy claims are not a completed implementation audit.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Normative answerability and many-hands responsibility should not be reduced to perceived blame shares. The proposed separate header/items improve conceptual clarity but still need validation and cannot establish effective reasons/remedy.

Unlike154’s fixed price-then-data sequence, this protocol plans balanced scenario orders and explicit null-equivalence checks. Neither design isolates its focal construct if scenario content varies in other material ways. Both measure hypothetical judgments rather than actual organizational/clinical behavior.

Human oversight is a configuration requiring real capacity, authority and context fit; a nominal surgeon review or rarely modified plan does not by itself prove controllability, automation bias or safe autonomy.

deferred.reason: A planned change in the loci of responsibility ratings, covered by blame/answerability notes. No new measured behavior or distinct synonym is warranted.
A proposed distribution index, not psychological diffusion or a new behavior. Requires explicit scale transformation and total-level interpretation.
Expected profile, not an observed named phenomenon; tasks and decisional configurations differ.

Useful named methodological leads. This protocol supplies exclusion criteria and possible artifacts rather than a dedicated original study or sufficient boundary against existing attention/evaluation concepts; consult the cited methods sources before adding broad new entries.
Background items and secondary literature leads, not separately validated mechanisms or new empirical findings here.

limitations: No cited primary paper or textbook becomes a completed read through this protocol. No automatic paper-count inflation, ethical/harm edges or yearly mention totals are added. Prototype methods must remain marked planned until a results source is read.
